findings.explanation: The Comb rule of RACONV omits the premise RACONV env (s1,s2). HOL4 requires both RACONV env (s1,s2) and RACONV env (t1,t2); Lean requires only the argument premise, so the function parts of two applications are unconstrained. For example, Lean derives ACONV (Comb (Const a ty) t) (Comb (Const b ty) t) for a ≠ b with t a Const, which HOL4 refutes. The weaker ACONV also makes the EQ_MP rule of proves too permissive.
findings.repair:
| Comb {env : List (term × term)} {s1 s2 t1 t2 : term} :
      RACONV env (s1, s2) → RACONV env (t1, t2) → RACONV env (Comb s1 t1, Comb s2 t2)
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntax

example (a b : Candle.mlstring) (ty : Candle.type) :
    Candle.RACONV [] (Candle.term.Comb (Candle.term.Const a ty) (Candle.term.Const a ty),
      Candle.term.Comb (Candle.term.Const b ty) (Candle.term.Const a ty)) :=
  Candle.RACONV.Comb Candle.RACONV.Const
findings.hol4_check: ∀a b ty. a ≠ b ⇒ ¬RACONV [] (Comb (Const a ty) (Const a ty), Comb (Const b ty) (Const a ty))
